specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** portability-barrier-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of ten reuse problems by the portability idea it breaks, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** The Portability Metric and the ten portability sections of this chapter (all defined above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each problem the learner commits one of ten ideas. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct idea column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the idea list is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A login problem and a lock-in problem are the same. (2) A link that fails is an embedding problem. (3) Offline access means no internet is ever needed. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a problem by the idea it breaks is an Understand-level action that connects a symptom to a check. Ten problems, one per idea, teach the learner to name what is actually wrong. **Content:** The ten ideas: Browser compatibility, No-login access, Iframe embedding, Link sharing, Export format, LMS import, LTI integration, Responsive layout, Offline access, Platform lock-in. The ten problems: | # | Problem shown to the learner | Correct idea | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The page works in one browser and shows an error in the others. | Browser compatibility | The page does not work across the main browsers. | | 2 | Visitors must create an account before they can see the first page. | No-login access | An account is a barrier to use. | | 3 | A teacher's course page shows a blank frame where the simulation should be. | Iframe embedding | The page cannot be shown inside another page. | | 4 | The address changes every time the page is opened, so a saved link fails. | Link sharing | There is no stable address to send. | | 5 | The only download is a file that opens in one company's program. | Export format | There is no open copy to keep. | | 6 | A teacher cannot bring the unit into her LMS as a package. | LMS import | The resource offers no way to import it. | | 7 | A quiz tool opened from the LMS cannot send scores back to the gradebook. | LTI integration | The tool and the LMS do not exchange information. | | 8 | On a phone the text is tiny and the right half of the page is cut off. | Responsive layout | The page does not adapt to the screen width. | | 9 | A field trip has no internet, and the resource offers no download. | Offline access | The resource cannot be used without a connection. | | 10 | The author's content exists only inside one company's service, with no export. | Platform lock-in | Leaving the platform would lose the content. | **Provenance:** The problems are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The ideas follow the chapter sections on each concept. **Rules:** Each problem has exactly one correct idea, and the ten ideas are all different. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one problem and the ten ideas. 2. The learner may open the idea list. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses an idea, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After problem 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 problems in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [idea]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This breaks [idea]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can name what stops a resource from traveling." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed problem. **Starting State:** The first problem and the ten ideas. The question shown is "Which portability idea does this break?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's ten ideas are browser compatibility, no-login access, iframe embedding, link sharing, export format, LMS import, LTI integration, responsive layout, offline access, and platform lock-in.
